definition: Protecting AI systems and their inputs, models, tools and data from attacks and misuse.
details: AI security spans prompt injection, model theft, data poisoning, supply-chain risk and abuse of agents with access to real systems. Frameworks such as the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications catalog the most common failure modes and defenses.
story: Picture guardrails on a mountain road — not there to slow you down on the straightaways, but to keep you from flying off the cliff. It is the habit of asking, before every launch, what could go wrong — and then doing something about it. Think of it as the quiet rule that a tool should be useful without being dangerous. It is the difference between “it works” and “it is safe to put in front of people.” That deliberate caution is AI Security.

citation.title: OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications
